title: GPU pool pressure: implement queue reservoir and preemptive drain strategy
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: During the 2025-02-12 capacity exhaustion event, long-running low-priority requests caused persistent queue buildup and prevented burst capacity from serving latency-sensitive traffic. This ticket implements a queue 'reservoir' (capacity reserved for high-priority routes), staged throttle bands, and a preemptive drain mechanism that moves old/low-priority items to deferred processing or cancels them when pressure crosses thresholds. The goal is to reduce user-facing 95th/99th latency regressions without aggressive autoscale churn.
acceptance_criteria: Reservoir implemented: at least one configurable reservoir per GPU pool that reserves 10-30% of in-flight slots for high-priority routes
Staged throttle bands deployed: new admission controller supports three bands (normal, pressure-warning, pressure-critical) with documented behaviors
Preemptive drain: requests older than X seconds or labeled low-priority are either deferred to a background worker or evicted according to policy; evictions produce observable metrics and traces
No observable increase in error-rate for P0 routes after rollout; 95th token latency for P0 routes improves by >= 20% under synthetic pressure tests
Playbook updated and an automated Canary run in CI that simulates queue pressure exists and passes

updates: 2025-02-20: Ticket created after postmortem review for 2025-02-12 capacity incident. Initial design proposal discussed in incident retro.

2025-02-22: Design workshop held — consensus to prioritize reservoir per-pool over global reservoir due to heterogeneous traffic patterns. Decided on three throttle bands and preemptive drain approach.
2025-02-24: Prototype admission-controller changes implemented in branch feature/queue-reservoir. Basic local unit tests green. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4612
2025-02-26: Telemetry schema proposed. Metric names and labels agreed: reservoir_fill_ratio{pool}, preemptive_evictions_total{priority,reason}.

2025-02-28: Maria rolled out a small canary (10% traffic) in staging. Observed expected drop in P0 95th latency under synthetic pressure. Noted a rare race when pool resizing occurs; backlog: add a resize-safe lock.
2025-03-03: Rajiv implemented deferred queue persistent marker to avoid double-processing; integrated with existing retry/backoff logic. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/worker/pull/128
2025-03-04: Telemetry dashboard draft at https://grafana.redwood.dev/d/queues/queue-reservoir. Zoe requested a heatmap for age-by-priority. Added to action items.

2025-03-05: QA running synthetic pressure tests in canary; initial pass successful for P0 latency. Preparing rollout plan for 25% -> 50% -> 100% with 2-hour observation windows. Updated ticket status to In Progress.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: aggressive eviction reduces latency but may starve batch/background workloads. To mitigate, we introduce deferred processing with best-effort background workers and quota tokens for long-running jobs.
We decided against immediate global admission hard-limits because different pools have different burst characteristics; per-pool reservoirs give better local control.
Follow-up item: explore integrating reservoir target with autoscaler signals so preemptive drain can trigger opportunistic scale-up with hysteresis (future ticket).
